quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest. Take time to stretch and relax, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: You are driving at night toward another vehicle. Your headlights:

options.text: Should be off. Use parking lights only.
Can be on high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when approaching or following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When making a right turn, you should not:

options.text: Turn too wide for your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn too wide for your lane.
questions.explanation: When turning right, slow down and signal at least 100 feet before the turn. Do not turn too wide, as this may hit other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:
questions.explanation: When being passed, yield to the other vehicle and do not increase your speed. Let the vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends.
Prepare for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Not turn on any vehicle lights.

questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beam headlights within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: A vehicle coming toward you at night has its high beams on. You cannot see the road ahead. You should:

options.text: Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.
Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to contact the police to determine if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight. You can only turn left when you can do so safely without affecting oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for a long time without scanning around you. This makes you zone out and increases your risk of crashing into vehicles that slow down or stop ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents or other unusual events causes traffic congestion. Avoid this behavior.

questions.question: You may drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway:

options.text: As long as you aren't driving.
If you are riding in the back seat.
If you are riding in the back of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to consume or have any alcoholic beverage while in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container in the driver or passenger areas of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: If moving with a stream of vehicles across railroad tracks, it is safe to stop on the tracks for a short time.
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Always make sure your entire vehicle can clear the tracks before crossing.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.
